title: dedicated-autoscaler-priority-routing-burst-util-reporting
author: Ethan Zhang
description:
Motivation: Dedicated customers have asked for stronger guarantees for multi-tenant fleets where business-critical routes must be protected during noisy neighbor or traffic spikes. This PR extends the dedicated autoscaler to support priority-based routing and burst token controls, and it improves utilization reporting to make per-priority economic tradeoffs visible to SREs and platform engineers.

What I changed (summary):
- Priority-aware autoscaler: added priority_weights and min_throughput_guarantee to fleet configs so higher-priority routes are guaranteed a minimum throughput when capacity is constrained.
- Burst token bucket per-priority: implemented per-priority token buckets with configurable burst_tokens and burst_recharge_rate. Burst usage is accounted and throttled separately from steady-state autoscale decisions.
- Smoother recharge and drain: updated tokenbucket smoothing algorithm to avoid short-lived spikes causing autoscaler thrash; introduced a 30s smoothing window and exponential backoff for recharge under sustained high load.
- Utilization reporting: new Prometheus metrics (redwood_dedicated_fleet_utilization_total, redwood_dedicated_priority_burst_usage, redwood_dedicated_min_throughput_guarantee_utilized) and dashboard panels. Historical per-priority utilization is now available in the console.
- Config API and validation: extended fleet API schema and CLI config to accept priority routing fields; added validation to prevent misconfiguration (sum of priority_weights must be > 0, min_throughput <= fleet_capacity).
- Backwards compatibility: default behavior is unchanged for fleets without priority config; autoscaler falls back to existing tokenbucket behavior.

Implementation notes:
- Core autoscaler changes are in pkg/autoscaler/fleet_manager.go and pkg/autoscaler/tokenbucket.go. Priority routing logic lives in pkg/routing/priority_router.go which is a thin layer used by the scaler and the request router.
- Metrics instrumentation added in internal/observability/prom.go and dashboards in infra/grafana/dedicated_utilization.json.
- Added unit tests and integration load tests in test/autoscaler and perf/benchmarks/dedicated-priority-routing.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests: 48 new unit tests covering tokenbucket, smoothing, and priority weight calculations.
- Integration: ran canary across two dedicated fleets in staging for 72 hours with synthetic traffic patterns (mixed high/low priority). No regressions observed in median latency; burst fairness improved for high-priority routes.
- Load tests: sustained 3x baseline traffic spike where burst_token consumption tripped gracefully and autoscaler added capacity without thrashing.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag (feature.dedicated_priority_routing) default off for existing accounts.
2) Enable for internal staging fleets and run canary for 72h.
3) Gradual enable for opt-in customers via console toggle.
4) After validation, enable by default with conservative defaults and release notes.

Related: ENG-2154 (priority autoscaling design), ENG-2199 (utilization reporting enhancements), SUP-4123 (customer request for throughput guarantees).

feat(routing): implement priority_router and integrate with scaler
perf(autoscaler): tokenbucket smoothing and exponential recharge backoff
docs(api): extend fleet API schema and CLI validation
obs(prom): expose per-priority utilization and burst metrics
tests: add unit and integration tests for priority routing and burst controls
review_comments: Maya Patel: Please add a migration note for existing fleet configs. What happens if min_throughput_guarantee is larger than current capacity?
Ethan Zhang: Replyed - validator prevents min_throughput > fleet_capacity and we default guarantee to 0 for existing fleets. Added note in docs and CLI validation.
Liam O'Connor: Can we ensure metrics cardinality stays low? Concerned about per-priority labels leading to explosion when customers create many priorities.

Ethan Zhang: Replyed - we aggregate metrics by priority tier and include a per-fleet summary only. Documented recommended limits and added a config cap (max_priorities_per_fleet) to prevent explosion.
Sofia Rivera: Tests look good. One nits: rename 'burst_recharge_rate' -> 'burst_recharge_per_sec' for clarity.
Ethan Zhang: Renamed config and updated docs/tests accordingly.
CI: initial build failed due to lint error in priority_router.go; fixed in second commit.
Maya Patel: Approve after resolving migration note and adding rollout steps.
release_notes:
- Add priority-based autoscaling for dedicated fleets with min throughput guarantees and per-priority burst token buckets.
- New Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboard panels for per-priority utilization and burst usage.
- Backwards compatible; feature gated behind feature.dedicated_priority_routing.
notes: Feature gated, opt-in rollout. Ops runbook updated under docs/ops/dedicated_autoscaler_priority.md. Monitoring alerts created: AW-FleetPriorityBurstHigh and AW-FleetGuaranteeViolation.
changelog_entry: Added priority routing and burst controls to the dedicated autoscaler; improved utilization reporting and observability.
